title: Understanding Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) in India
description: Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) are privately pooled investment vehicles for sophisticated investors seeking diverse opportunities. SEBI classifies AIFs i.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment for an AIF?
faq.a: The minimum investment for most Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) is ₹1 crore. However, for employees or directors of the AIF or its manager, the minimum investment is ₹25 lakhs.

Yes, all Alternative Investment Funds operating in India must be registered with and regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are permitted to invest in SEBI-registered AIFs, subject to compliance with FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act) regulations and specific terms of the fund.

faq.q: What are the main risks of investing in AIFs?
faq.a: Key risks include illiquidity (long lock-in periods), higher investment risk due to unlisted or complex assets, potential for capital loss, dependence on fund manager expertise, and complex fee structures.
AIF investments are generally illiquid. They typically involve long lock-in periods, often ranging from 5 to 10 years, and redemption options are limited, unlike mutual funds.

faq.q: Are AIFs suitable for all investors?
faq.a: No, AIFs are suitable only for sophisticated investors, such as High Net Worth Individuals (HNIs) and institutions, who have a high-risk appetite, a substantial investable surplus, and a long-term investment horizon.

faq.q: What is a Private Placement Memorandum (PPM)?
faq.a: A Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) is a detailed document provided by an AIF to prospective investors. It outlines the fund's investment strategy, risks, fee structure, terms and conditions, and other essential information.
